title: THE BODY
blurb: Hands, eyes, feet and what goes wrong with them.

radicals.name: HAND
radicals.origin: 手 is a hand with its fingers spread. On the left it slims down to three strokes, and the last one flicks upward.
radicals.clue: things you do with your hands
ex: printed on doors all over China
on the other side of the same doors
radicals.watch: 扌 is the busiest radical in everyday Chinese. Look-alike: 牜 (cow), as in 物 and 特, has an extra stroke at the top left.

radicals.name: EYE
radicals.origin: An eye, turned on its side so it stands tall. The two lines inside were once the pupil.
ex: a hand 手 shading the eye
radicals.watch: Count the lines inside. 目 (eye) has two, 日 (sun) has one, and 自 (self) is an eye with a tick on top.

radicals.name: BODY
radicals.origin: 肉 means meat or flesh. Written small it came to look exactly like 月, the moon, so the two now share one shape.
radicals.watch: The same shape is sometimes the real moon. A rough rule: on the left or at the bottom it is usually flesh (脸, 背). On the right it is usually the moon (明 bright, 期 a period of time).

radicals.name: FOOT
radicals.origin: 足 is a kneecap 口 above a foot. On the left its last stroke kicks up to make room for the rest of the character.
radicals.watch: On its own, 足 means foot (足球, football) and also enough. Do not mix it up with 走 (to walk), which is a separate radical.

radicals.name: SICKNESS
radicals.origin: The old picture is a person lying on a bed. It never stands alone: it only ever wraps the top and left of another part.
ex: the radical is named after this one
once a sign of poor health
radicals.watch: Look-alike: 广 (a shelter), as in 店 (shop) and 床 (bed). 疒 has two extra dots on its left edge.
